afc5d91188.q: Why do bond portfolio values decline when interest rates rise?
afc5d91188.a: When interest rates rise, bond values fall temporarily because existing bonds paying lower rates become less attractive than newly issued bonds at higher rates. If you buy a two-year bond at 4.25% and rates rise to 4.75%, your bond's market value drops below 100 cents on the dollar, though you'll get full value at maturity if you hold it.
